author: ojiudezue
title: Room dialogs: enumeration vs automation; per-light roles, no new light timers
summary: Devices/Sensors only list and classify; every 'which ones should URA act on' choice lives in its behaviour step. Lighting becomes per-light roles (on entry, only-when-dark, night lights, leave on when empty, alert) with one room 'counts as empty' timeout; leave-on is the per-light exemption; an optional per-room switch turns leave-on lights off at Away; vacancy off applies to every non-leave-on light and ends the manual hold. Darkness = room lux, else sun at -6 deg (P0), borrowed lux P1.
why: Operator: room dialog is 'the absolute core of URA' and 'a power-user mess'; roles were global per room and misfiled in Devices (Night Lights, Auto/Manual devices). Operator rejected an extra light timer ('I don't want to add an extra timer(s)'): the occupancy timeout already is the light wait, and a second one makes 'which timer turned it off' unanswerable. Sun fallback is an intended change that only touches 3 rooms (no/offline lux).
implications: Builds in slices on feature/room-lighting-roles (A resolver + B darkness done, held); C (light manual hold + URA-wide write mark across 10 writers + room light switch) is the delicate slice. Any new room field must be a role in a behaviour step, never a new timer. Occupancy timeout still doubles as the sensor-trust window (2x) — decouple internally later.
revisit_trigger: If a real room needs lights to linger past 'empty', add an optional extra-on default 0; if the write mark misclassifies an alert flash as manual.
